look_here_first: PURPLE THREEAWN = perennial tuft with basal narrow inrolled leaves. On ONE mature spikelet the LOWER GLUME is usually markedly SHORTER than the UPPER and typically ONE-veined; Kew's example is ~6–8 versus 11–15 mm, BUT some varieties (notably var. longiseta) have a much longer upper glume (14–25 mm). Oldfield is an annual with BOTH glumes near-equal and lower with 3–7 veins. Measure both glumes on one spikelet and inspect crown before deciding; purple color and absolute upper-glume length alone are unreliable.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora; Williamson — detailed county treatment of A. purpurea var. purpurea; Travis — USDA ARS herbarium collections from Austin/Travis County.

best_field_traits: Count THREE AWNS arising from ONE fertile lemma, not from three independent florets. This recognizes Aristida GENUS only.
PURPLE is a PERENNIAL: a persistent dense old basal tuft/crown with numerous thin, often inrolled BASAL leaves; photograph rooted crown from side.

Main species test: lower glume generally substantially shorter than upper, typically ONE lower-glume vein; Kew broad treatment illustrates 6–8 mm lower vs 11–15 mm upper but varietal upper glumes can reach 14–25 mm (var. longiseta) — DO NOT treat 15 mm as a species-wide cutoff.
Texas forms often have conspicuous relatively LONG hairs around true leaf COLLAR; take a true collar macro, not a stem-node photograph. Other Aristida forms can overlap.
Open or nodding often purplish panicles and long near-equal 3 awns help only as supporting pattern. Purple color NOT reliable.
Oldfield THREEAWN: annual freely branched wiry stems, very long near equal glumes (~18–25 mm) and multiple lower-glume veins.
Very short tightly coiled central awn is churchmouse THREEAWN; contracted short-glumed uneven-awned head raises slimspike THREEAWN (comparison-only).
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use glume relative length and LOWER glume vein count on a mature intact spikelet: A. purpurea has ~6–8 mm lower and ~11–15 mm upper (1-veined lower), while A. oligantha has ~18–25 mm subequal glumes (3–7-veined lower). Confirm a perennial vs annual basal crown; panicle shape and awn color are supporting only.

comparisons.key_distinctions: PURPLE A. purpurea: persistently perennial root crown, lower glume notably shorter than upper, usually 1 lower vein; lengths vary by variety including var. longiseta. OLDFIELD A. oligantha: annual, mature lower AND upper glumes near-equal and rather long (often 18–25 mm) with lower 3–7 veins. Use a matched dissection of ONE intact spikelet, not color, absolute upper glume length or openness.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare one intact mature spikelet and the basal crown, not the purple seedhead color.
field_matrix.this_species: PURPLE perennial old tuft and rolled mostly basal leaves; LOWER glume typically about HALF upper (6–8 vs 11–15 mm), usually 1 lower-glume vein.
field_matrix.look_alike: OLD FIELD is annual, much more freely branched, glumes much longer and NEARLY EQUAL (~18–25 mm) with 3–7 lower veins.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Shorter lower glume + 1 vein + perennial tuft → PURPLE candidate; long equal multi-veined + annual branching → OLDFIELD candidate.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Look at central awn base on an intact mature floret.
field_matrix.this_species: Oldfield has 3 spreading long, roughly equal awns typically 30–70 mm.
field_matrix.look_alike: Churchmouse has very short awns: central ~3–8 mm with a basal spiral, lateral ~1–4 mm.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Short coiled central awn means investigate churchmouse, not oldfield.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare whole panicle shape, glume length and central versus lateral awns.
field_matrix.this_species: Oldfield typically has open sparse branches and long subequal glumes 18–25 mm.
field_matrix.look_alike: Slimspike is annual with relatively contracted head, short glumes (~3–9 mm in Texas regional descriptions) and central awn longer than lateral, no strong central basal spiral.
field_matrix.quick_rule: A narrow compact short-glumed inflorescence with uneven shorter awns needs slimspike comparison.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Inspect awns arising from ONE fertile lemma instead of counting surrounding spikelets.
field_matrix.this_species: Aristida typically has THREE lemma awns.
field_matrix.look_alike: Many muhlys or needlegrasses bear a single awn or none; gramas have characteristic branches of many spikelets.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Enter the Aristida key only after seeing awns on one lemma.

not_reliable_alone: Three awns is GENUS, not species.
Open versus narrow panicle without mature glumes.
Annual appearance from a detached stalk.
Broken lower glume or glume measurements including awn.
Long awn length alone, which overlaps varieties.

diagnostic_photo_polish.measured_variety_caution_20261022: VARIETY / MEASUREMENT CAUTION: Kew GrassBase's A. purpurea broad-description lower glume 6–8 mm and upper 11–15 mm are a useful example, NOT a strict limit for every variety. A. purpurea var. longiseta can have upper glumes 14–25 mm (PNW revised flora), and an independently measured var. longiseta specimen had lower 11 mm, upper 20 mm (Schweich collection 1140). Use RELATIVE shorter lower glume + typically one lower vein, confirmed permanent perennial base and variety-aware local key. DO NOT reject purple or declare oldfield solely because an upper glume measures ~20 mm. A. oligantha's character is long NEAR-EQUAL 18–25 mm glumes AND a lower glume with 3–7 veins; photograph BOTH same-spikelet glumes.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Purple threeawn — start at basal crown then lower glume
steps: One long AWN is arrowed on a licensed actual purple-threeawn spikelet; find three awn branches emerging from a SINGLE lemma in a separate inspected specimen.
Photograph rooted PERENNIAL tuft with many fine inrolled BASAL leaves; don't infer perennial crown from one isolated flowering stem.
Dissect ONE ripe spikelet on a millimeter ruler, preserving both glumes; lower usually about HALF upper in Kew broad description.
Backlight LOWER glume to confirm ONE main vein; compare oldfield's 3–7 and larger near-equal glumes.
At a true LEAF COLLAR look for conspicuous long hairs in local purple threeawn, but do not use that alone to confirm species.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use lower/upper glume RATIO, lower vein count, and rooted perennial crown; do not identify by purplish fall awns alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Variety-aware key: Kew glume dimensions are typical, not fixed. Var. longiseta upper glumes 14–25 mm overlap absolute oldfield sizes; compare LOWER/UPPER ratio and lower glume veins with rooted crown. Need true matched local macro.
